## TL;DR
Task branches now contain only their own task's files. The engineer self-check checkpoint commit stages only the task's own files plus source changes, a guarded cleanup at handoff restores other tasks' `work/` and `work/reports/` files from main, and the landing preflight names the offending files and cause in plain English.

## Work and rationale
An audit of the server paths that can write another task's bookkeeping into a task worktree found the WIP checkpoint commit (staging with a blanket add) and the merge-of-main sync as the leak points. The checkpoint commit now excludes `work/*.md` for other ids and `work/reports/<other id>/**`. Before the review lock, handoff restores any such files from main through a normal commit that review tolerates as bookkeeping, and reports what it restored instead of failing. `repoos landable` and the handoff report name the files and cause. Tests cover a dirty worktree producing a clean checkpoint, a drifted branch being healed at handoff, and the preflight passing afterwards. `docs/agent-workflow-rules.md`, `docs/close-out-pipeline.md` and AGENTS.md describe the rule.

## Approaches tried
Restoring files by hand each round (what engineers did before), then blocking the leak at the source and healing existing drift at handoff.

## Challenges and blockers
Several handoffs failed on `A check is running` collisions with the engineer's own check and on a recorded identical check failure for an unchanged tip, even though a full local and remote check passed. A new commit was needed to request a fresh validation.

## Key learnings
Fix the source of the leak and heal drift at handoff, because per-round manual restores are what wasted engineer time. A refused handoff on an identical tip needs a new commit, and that is now documented.
